name: tag_create

path.udtDefinitionNamespace: only under an explicit _types_ allowlist entry

nativeOutcome: one system.tag.configure call per item; its single QualityCode is that item's outcome, and Observed state never decides success

preconditionToken.why: D30 2 gives tag_create no Precondition token: the caller's own earlier read cannot exist, because the target must not. The concurrency rule is D11's collision rule instead — the target must be absent, and the handler fixes collisionPolicy=Abort so a race that creates it anyway aborts rather than overwrites.
preconditionToken.existingTargetCheck: system.tag.exists(path) for every item before any item executes

preflight: input, reserved provider and Target allowlist for every item before any item executes, with no rollback

runtimeTargetPolicy.allowlistMatch: provider-qualified config path prefix at segment boundaries; explicit * allows every provider but never a UDT definition
runtimeTargetPolicy.reservedProviderRefusal: permission_denied before Preflight, whatever the allowlist says, including an explicit *

targetPath.form: <provider>Tag, <provider>Folder or <provider>Folder/Tag, and <provider>_types_/... for a UDT definition
targetPath.noWildcard: a config target is one exact path: a *, ? or : anywhere in it is invalid_argument
targetPath.leaf: the target's last segment is the definition name sent to system.tag.configure, and a config that names a different one is invalid_argument

udtDefinitionTargets: an explicit _types_ allowlist entry only: a target inside the _types_ namespace is refused with permission_denied unless an entry that itself names _types_ matches it, so a bare * does not cover a UDT definition (D30 6)
existingTargetFails: conflict (details.items[].reason = targetExists): D30 2 and D11 give a create no Precondition token, so an existing target is the collision the caller is told about, and no item is executed
neverOverwrites: the handler sends collisionPolicy=Abort, so a target that appears between the Preflight existence check and the dispatch aborts that item's configure instead of being overwritten; nothing is ever replaced

refusedConfigKeys.value: invalid_argument (configValueIsAControlWrite): a Tag value write is tag_write's, and this Tool belongs to the CONFIG class
refusedConfigKeys.tags: invalid_argument (configNestedTagsNotAllowed): a child is its own target, so it is created as its own item
refusedConfigKeys.name: invalid_argument (configNameChangeNotAllowed): the target path names the node, and a different name is tag_rename's

ambiguousOutcomeScope: an item whose own dispatch raised is outcome_unknown and ends the batch (later items are not_executed); an item whose dispatch answered an unattributable QualityCode is outcome_unknown and the batch continues. Nothing is replayed

existenceCheck.call: system.tag.exists(path) for every item, before any item executes
existenceCheck.why: a Gateway answers system.tag.getConfiguration for a path that is not there with a synthesized default node, so the configuration read alone cannot tell the caller whether the target is already taken; the ticket #10 live run recorded the same synthesized node on 8.3.8 and 8.3.9
existenceCheck.present: conflict (details.items[].reason = targetExists), and nothing is dispatched
existenceCheck.unanswered: upstream_error (reasons existenceCheckFailed / existenceCheckIndeterminate): a Gateway that raises or answers something that is not a boolean is never read as absent
existenceCheck.observedReadBacks: the provider export is the independent presence check the harness uses

inputBounds.hardItemsPolicyRule: a deployment may raise the 20-target default through the Runtime Target Policy and never above the 100-target hard ceiling

observedState: the created node's own tag_get_config read: `system.tag.getConfiguration(path, false, false)`, published with the D30 2 fingerprint of that read. It is Observed state and never decides success, and the fingerprint is the token the caller's next tag_update/tag_delete would use
deniedMutationAudit: after a usable Policy is read, a refused Target and a refused existence check each produce one `decision` row and no dispatch; `off` records nothing, and `required` refuses the call when the denial row cannot be written
outcomePreservation: a dispatched batch reports its per-item Native outcomes whatever the Observed-state budget or the serializer does; an Observed configuration that cannot be returned is an explicit `limit_exceeded` observed error, and the result is re-rendered without the Observed state rather than replacing the outcomes
